exposure: pelvic organ prolapse severity (POP-Q stage II-IV)
cohort: The study included 33 postmenopausal women with symptomatic pelvic organ prolapse (POP-Q stage II or higher) matched with 33 postmenopausal women without POP.
finding: No statistically significant difference in tenascin-X expression was found between postmenopausal women with and without POP, although it was significantly more expressed in cases with severe prolapse (POP-Q stage IV) compared with moderate prolapse stages.
